prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my scientific case for B044 is unchanged and I no longer see it as one half of a possible pairing. The chain is complete and independently confirmed: proglucagon processing, identification of the truncated active peptide, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and effects on appetite and gastric emptying in humans, receptor biology, and then randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The field is mature, the mechanism is stable, and the benefit to patients is large. Holst (human physiology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor actions, translation) and Mojsov (the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) each cover a separable and necessary step. The citation should name the physiology and the active form and say that it enabled therapy, so that the therapeutic consequence is stated without crediting drug design as a discovery.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. The supplied credit list is not the full historical record: Habener's contribution to proglucagon and GLP-1 work is outside the ballot names, Mojsov's priority is publicly contested, and I cannot settle it from the committee materials alone. The three-person cap leaves out Knudsen, whose long-acting analogue design reached patients, and a discovery citation can look as if it ignores that step. A second part would have to be built from names that each carry an attribution gap of their own, and it would use up the cap. I treat these as real costs of the preferred configuration, not as reasons to change it.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps B012 (Mori and Walter) as her first alternative, calls it the cleanest attribution on the list, and says a prize on B044 with three laureates is cleaner than a four-person one that adds industrial drug development.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and in round 1 I raised pairing B044 with B012. I now withdraw that as my preferred design. A second part would have to fit under the three-person cap across the whole prize, which GLP-1 already uses in full, so adding Mori and Walter would mean dropping one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, and I cannot defend that on the science. B012 has the cleanest credit, but its clinical consequence is still developing, and I do not think that justifies reducing a mature and fully confirmed discovery. I leave B012 out of my alternatives for the same reason I would not want it to displace the stronger clinical cases in a later year.

responses.point: El-Manira asks whether a single-part prize is stronger than pairing B044 with CAR-T (B018), and notes that the best alternatives each carry a clearer attribution problem than B044 does (Eshhar missing from CAR-T, six credited names for three seats in optogenetics).
responses.response: My answer is that the single part is stronger. The cap is the decisive arithmetic: a CAR-T part could only be added by taking a seat from the GLP-1 trio. I also agree with your assessment of B018. The supplied names are June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, and Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is outside them, so a CAR-T trio would still leave a gap in the credit. I keep B018 as my first alternative because its clinical effect is the most firmly established among the options, but I would not trade it against any member of the GLP-1 set.

responses.point: Perlmann leaves Knudsen out on the grounds of the three-person limit and the discovery focus, worries that the prize may be read as honouring a commercial product, and doubts that a second part is advisable.
responses.response: I agree that a second part is not advisable here. On Knudsen, I still hold that the half-life extension was decisive for the therapy and that she would be a legitimate laureate under a four-person rule. Under the cap I would leave her out and say so openly in the committee record, as the chair has also asked, so that the omission reads as a consequence of the limit and the discovery framing. To answer your concern that this honours a product, I would anchor the citation in physiology and the active peptide, which is where the three named people made their contributions, and not in any one drug.

responses.point: The chair asks what primary-record evidence supports crediting Mojsov at full weight and how Habener's absence should be recorded, and asks whether optogenetics is an eligible discovery with a defensible subset of three.
responses.response: I can only answer from the committee materials, which do not settle priority. I rely on the supplied record that Mojsov identified and characterised the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, which is a separable step from Holst's human physiology and Drucker's biology. I would credit her at full weight, while saying in the record that Habener's proglucagon and peptide work is acknowledged but outside the supplied ballot names, so the committee cannot vote on him. On B001, optogenetics is eligible as a method-driven discovery with a precedent in earlier prizes, but channelrhodopsin function and neuronal implementation are separable achievements, and any trio from the six names would omit credible contributors. That is why it stays a lower-ranked alternative.

responses.point: Sandberg prefers a single-achievement prize because GLP-1 is already broad and each of the three people contributed a necessary step.
responses.response: We agree, and this round has made me firmer on it. Where I now differ slightly is on Knudsen. You mention that she could be left to other recognition, but I would not treat that as a reason for the omission. I would treat it as a cost of the cap and state it in the record. I stay with B018 and B001 as alternatives, and in the earlier TOR exchange I still hold that Hall and Schreiber hold the foundational steps, so B013 is not among my alternatives.

uncertainties: How credit for the active GLP-1 peptide should be divided among Mojsov, Habener, Holst and Drucker, given that Habener is not a ballot name and priority cannot be settled from the committee materials.
Whether leaving out Knudsen is defensible in the record and citation, or whether the three-person cap makes a different configuration fairer.
Whether a fair CAR-T trio can be built without Eshhar, and whether Rosenberg belongs in a CAR-specific citation, if B018 is ever needed as a fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict applies to any shortlisted candidate. My documented co-authorship (spatial transcriptomics, Science 2016; prior joint work with Rickard Sandberg, also disclosed by him) does not involve any shortlisted name, and shared institution or topic is not treated as a personal tie. I do not seek recusal.
